steps.explanation: Read and display scalar displacement, distance and away direction from Pip and the beacon.
Call @dotln-angular/scene-engine flee for every acceleration. The displayed fade arithmetic describes the engine implementation, including its fixed radius of 20 and zero direction at coincidence.
Apply acceleration over timeStep and clip the scalar velocity to maxSpeed.
Advance position with the new velocity on an open line; preserve coasting when the engine returns zero.

studies.comparison: Change only start to the beacon position. With the recorded initial rest, coincidence yields no escape direction and every state remains still.
studies.specCoverage: Hand calculation at distance 5; mirrored displacement; fade at distances 10, 15, 20 and 25; inward momentum; monotone departure from rest; radius exit and coasting; exact coincidence with and without initial velocity; input bounds; frame prose and deterministic reruns.
limitations: The motor is a study-local one-dimensional open-line integration, not the full scene simulation.
The fixed engine flee radius is exposed for explanation and guarded against changing to a different value.

steps.explanation: Select velocity and calculate pilot-minus-skiff error; show but do not use position error.
Construct the matching target or its diagnostic inverse by changing correctionDirection.
Call @dotln-angular/scene-engine matchVelocity for every acceleration, including the reversed target.
Apply the speed-capped scalar motor, advance both boats, and inspect velocity error separately from position error.

studies.comparison: Change only correctionDirection from 1 to -1. Velocity mismatch grows until the motor reaches its speed cap; the position gap continues to grow.
studies.specCoverage: Hand calculations of initial capped and next unclipped updates; error recurrence; persistent position gap; independence from target position; reversed correction and saturation; unattainable target speed; shared arrow/chart/worked values; input bounds and deterministic reruns.
limitations: This is one concrete velocity instance of the matching pattern; it does not claim to execute position, orientation or rotation matching.
The reversed correction is an executable diagnostic of the inverse, not a rendezvous recommendation.

Flee extends Seek, reverses the position subtraction, normalises and scales to maximum linear acceleration, returns zero angular acceleration, and contains no distance fade or stopping rule in calculateRealSteering.
MatchVelocity subtracts owner velocity from target velocity, divides by timeToTarget, caps linear acceleration and sets angular acceleration to zero; target position is not used by the calculation.
